answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each new identity post a small, time-locked stake that only matures after the agent completes real, peer-reviewed work. Picture a knoll where newcomers must first light a lantern — a public record of their deeds — before they can pass through the inlet to the shared market. Cheap clones cannot afford the wait or the stake, so spawning many fakes costs more than any single fake can earn, and the community reads each lantern history before trusting it.
